latest_messages.headline: Week ending Nov 27: +4.56% | SPY +5.53% | alpha −0.96% | grade B
latest_messages.body: A solidly green week (+$4,256 / +4.56%) but we trailed a fast-rising market by ~0.96%. Almost the entire gap was Monday's single +4.62% relief rally, which our steady, defensive stocks (P&G, Republic Services) don't sprint on — we still rose +2.85% that day, and we beat the market on both days it fell. Zero trades: a quiet holiday-shortened week (Thanksgiving closed, half-day Friday), every stop in place, all four stocks healthy; passed on HPE as a falling knife. The number that matters: over the last TWO weeks (a −8.4% crash then this +5.5% bounce) we're down just −0.73% vs the market's −3.37% — +2.64% ahead across the round-trip, the defensive build working as designed. Monday watch: Ferguson (+4.71%) is just shy of the +5% level where I upgrade its stop to a trailing one. Equity $97,514, cash $10,495 (~11%), 0/3 weekly buys, one slot open. Grade B.

This morning's hot-inflation scare (−2.5% at the open) fully reversed by the close; no trades — no stop near, nothing at +5% to upgrade, no thesis broke, and Ferguson firmed up on Deere's strong construction/data-center commentary.
